text:
julia: Team — BetaBank POC hitting 500/503s under demo load. They ramped to ~900 concurrent streams. seeing intermittent 5xxs and some clients got abrupt closes. env: dedicated-eu-central, pool: bank-poc, model: redwood-13b-quant. anyone awake to help?

ops-bot: [ALERT] 1789012345 - pool=bank-poc experiencing surge_errors=5xx (window=60s). autoscale: replicas=3 pending_scale_up.

anish: I'm on it. Can you share one failing response and any proxy logs?

julia: pasted a sample failed response:
HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error
X-Redwood-Error: accept_loop_overflow
Connection: close

proxy logs show a lot of 502/504s upstream.

dave: infra logs from runtime:
```
runtime: accept() failed: ECONNABORTED
queue_manager: request_queue length=10240 dropped=1200
worker[5] memory: rss=62GB, reserved_kv=18GB
autoscaler: scale_up scheduled -> replicas=6 (cooldown 60s)
```

nina: looks like request queue overflow plus workers under memory pressure. Quant 13b can push per-worker memory high when many concurrent long streams are active. any token-length stats?

julia: most test sessions use streaming with ~800 avg tokens, a few with 2500.

anish: short-term tactics to stop immediate 5xxs:
- enable proxy buffering (buffer requests up to 5s) to smooth bursts
- set per-client concurrency limit (e.g., max_concurrency=50) to avoid noisy neighbor in demo
- activate model-fallback rule to redwood-7b-quant for overload responses
- set route circuit-breaker to return 429 when queue full (instead of 500)

Commands to run now:
```
redwoodctl pools patch bank-poc --proxy-buffering true --proxy-buffer-max-ms 5000
redwoodctl routes patch bank-poc-route --max-concurrency-per-client 50 --circuit-breaker-mode 429
redwoodctl routes patch bank-poc-route --fallback-model redwood-7b-quant
```

dave: applying proxy buffering and concurrency cap now. also forcing autoscaler aggressive policy for this pool (min_replicas=5, scale_cooldown=20s).

(operations)

ops-bot: [INFO] 1789012402 - proxy_buffering enabled for pool=bank-poc by dave
ops-bot: [INFO] 1789012410 - route bank-poc-route updated: max_concurrency_per_client=50 circuit_breaker=429 fallback=redwood-7b-quant
ops-bot: [INFO] 1789012425 - pool bank-poc scaled 3 -> 5 (requested by dave)

julia: after changes error rate dropped but still seeing 502s for long-run sessions. buffer helps, but worker OOMs still occur under the heaviest tails.

anish: immediate customer-facing ask: can BetaBank throttle long sessions or cap token_size per request? Recommend clients set streaming_max_tokens=1500 or split large inputs. We'll send sample Retry-After-friendly client snippet.

nina: I'll send a safe client template with exponential backoff and Retry-After handling. Also suggest they prefer the 7b fallback for bulk ingestion jobs.

dave: for infra follow-ups: prewarm extra workers before demo start, enable progressive KV eviction, and add a soft token cap per worker to refuse >2000 tokens. I'll open infra task.

julia: customer is okay with routing heavy jobs to 7b for now. they want ETA on full fix (no need to change client).

anish: timeline: short-term (applied) should keep tail errors low within 8-12m. medium-term (prewarm + KV eviction + lower batch_latency) 2-3 days to implement and test. long-term: autoscale prediction + warm pools for scheduled demos.

(8 minutes later)

julia: update — error rate fell from 9% -> 1.1% in last 5m. BetaBank confirms demo continues. thanks.

ops-bot: [RESOLVED] 1789012670 - surge mitigated on pool=bank-poc.

(POSTMORTEM NOTE)
anish: root cause: demo-induced request burst with many long-sequence streaming sessions filled accept queue; runtime workers experienced KV allocation pressure -> memory oversubscription and accept-loop failures -> 5xx. Primary mitigations: proxy buffering, per-client concurrency limits, fallback to smaller model, aggressive autoscale and min_replicas bump. Action items: 1) infra ticket for prewarm & KV eviction, 2) route defaults for POC pools (lower batch latency, circuit breaker 429), 3) docs for customers on token caps and Retry-After handling.
